title: grpc_deadline plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `grpc_deadline` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component GrpcDeadlineConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

GrpcDeadlineConfig.description: Plugin: grpc_deadline — Manages the grpc-timeout metadata header. Supports all gRPC timeout units (H, M, S, m, u, n). At least one effective rule is required. When both deadline values are configured, default_deadline_ms must be less than or equal to max_deadline_ms, and headroom_ms must be less than max_deadline_ms; runtime validation enforces these cross-field relationships. Caps compose across instances independently of their order: a default injected by one instance is still clamped by another instance's max_deadline_ms. Malformed or zero client values never pass through verbatim: an enforced fallback deadline is rewritten onto the outbound header and invalid client values set bounded transaction-log metadata grpc_timeout_invalid=true. That metadata and grpc_adjusted_deadline_ms are recorded at request receipt, so they are present even when the request is rejected before the backend hook runs.

max_deadline_ms.description: Cap incoming deadlines to this value (milliseconds)

default_deadline_ms.description: Inject grpc-timeout when client omits it

headroom_ms.description: Fixed margin (milliseconds) reserved from a client-supplied grpc-timeout after every cap. Both the gateway's own RPC deadline and the forwarded grpc-timeout end this much earlier than the client's, so the gateway's DEADLINE_EXCEEDED reaches the client before the client's own deadline cancels the call. The remaining budget is floored at 1 ms. An injected default_deadline_ms is not reduced. Multiple instances reserve the largest configured value once. Must be less than max_deadline_ms when both are set.

subtract_gateway_processing.description: Plugin-checkpoint remaining-budget control. When true, the plugin writes remaining receipt-anchored milliseconds into grpc-timeout and grpc_adjusted_deadline_ms, and rejects with gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (status 4) if that remaining time is already zero. Backend H2/H3 dispatch always rewrites grpc-timeout to the remaining absolute budget independently of this flag.

reject_no_deadline.description: Reject requests missing a positive grpc-timeout. Takes precedence over default_deadline_ms. Native H2/H3 gRPC clients receive HTTP 200 with a non-OK grpc-status in the trailers-only header block; the internal plugin rejection status is not exposed as HTTP 400.
